subject: Dedicated capacity: Amphora multi-year ramp / prepay discussion
messages:
From: Ellie Barnes <ellie@amphora.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Amphora Procurement <procurement@amphora.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial capacity ask — ramped reserved GPU pool (multi-year)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the KV cache behavior. We are finalizing forecasted capacity needs and want to get a hard view from Redwood on multi-year reserved capacity pricing and how a phased ramp would work. High level:

- Peak target: ~24 A100-equivalent GPUs (TPM workload) by the end of year 2 (18 months to peak).
- Start: small production slice (4 GPUs) in month 1 to validate models.
- Ramp cadence: ideally in 3-6 month increments, but we can be flexible if there are pricing incentives for larger prepay.
- Need guidance on prepay options: annual prepay vs multi-year prepay, and how discounts scale with staged adds.

Attached is our demand forecast (Amphora_Demand_Forecast_Q1-Q4.pdf). Could you share a proposal that shows: a) a staircase-style ramp (committed slices over time), b) pricing for annual prepay vs 3-year prepay, c) overage rates and early termination terms?

We'd like to lock something in by mid-December to align with procurement planning. Open to a short call next week to run through numbers.

Best,
Ellie Barnes
Head of Infrastructure
Amphora AI

--
Attachments: Amphora_Demand_Forecast_Q1-Q4.pdf (application/pdf, 278KB)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@amphora.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — ramped reserved GPU pool (multi-year)

Ellie — thanks for the forecast and the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass term sheet (Redwood_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf) that maps to the staircase ramp you described. Highlights up front:

- Proposed operational ramp (staircase):
  * Month 1 (baseline): 4 GPUs reserved (initial slice)
  * Months 4 and 7: add 6 GPUs each (total 16 by month 7)
  * Month 12: add 8 GPUs (peak 24 by month 12) with option to defer final slice to month 18 with no penalty

- Prepay / discount framework:
  * Annual prepay (pay-as-annual): 10% off list on committed units, paid at start of each 12-month period.
  * 3-year prepay (one-time upfront): tiered discounts — 15% Y1 equivalent, 18% Y2 equivalent, 22% Y3 equivalent (effective blended).
  * If Amphora elects to prepay >=70% of forecasted peak in year 1, additional one-time credit equal to 5% of year-1 fees applied as account credit.

- Flex provisions: quarterly true-ups (usage-based) and short-term burst capacity available at negotiated overage rate (list * 1.6).
- SLAs: standard Dedicated SLA (99.9% uptime) with credits for sustained outages; see term sheet for definitions and latency SLOs.

Open items we want to resolve with you on a call: exact billing cadence (annual vs quarterly true-up), acceptance of the prepay credit structure, and whether you need an onramp protection clause (a defined minimum commit for year 1 to ensure capacity reservation).

If this looks directionally correct, I'll involve billing/legal and we can produce a DocuSign-ready term sheet. Proposed times for a short sync: Tue 11/24 10–11 PT, Wed 11/25 2–3 PT.

Thanks — Neha
Head, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)

--
Attachments: Redwood_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 46KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@amphora.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — ramped reserved GPU pool (multi-year)

Quick note from product/finance perspective —

Neha, nice baseline. A couple of tweaks we typically recommend for smoothing risk vs price:

- Consider a frontloaded deposit option (higher prepay in year 1) in exchange for a one-time accelerated discount (we can offer additional 5% effective discount if Amphora prepays >= 60% of 24-GPU peak in year 1). That helps our capacity planning and gives Amphora predictable unit economics.
- Alternative: staggered commitment with quarterly ramp triggers tied to usage thresholds (e.g., add next slice when 72-hour p50 utilization > 65%). This keeps Amphora flexible but reduces our inventory risk.

If Amphora prefers smoothing of cash flows, the hybrid approach (partial prepay + quarterly true-ups) usually balances outcomes. Rishi — happy to drop the proposed math in the term sheet if you want me to.

LA
Product Partnerships (Redwood)

From: Sam Cho <samc@amphora.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Ellie Barnes <ellie@amphora.ai>, Amphora Procurement <procurement@amphora.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — ramped reserved GPU pool (multi-year)

Neha — thanks for the detailed sheet. A few procurement items and requests from our CFO:

- Amphora can’t do heavy frontloading in year 1 — cash runway and customer milestones require smoothing. We prefer an annual payment schedule with even spread across quarters.
- We can accept a modest prepay (25% of year-1 committed fees) as a deposit to secure the initial slice.
- We need the ramp to be operationally flexible: allow deferral of the month-12 add by up to 6 months without penalty, provided quarterly true-ups are met.
- Request clarification on the overage rate formula and whether reserved capacity can be partially reassigned across projects (we have multiple teams that will share the pool).

Attached: procurement_questions_amphora.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 18KB) — includes standard procurement checklist and PO timing.

Can we meet Fri 12/4 to finalize the compromise?

— Sam
VP, Finance Ops, Amphora

--

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Sam Cho <samc@amphora.ai>, Ellie Barnes <ellie@amphora.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask — ramped reserved GPU pool (multi-year)

Sam / Ellie — thanks for the candid constraints. We can move to a compromise that preserves predictability for both sides. Summary of the proposed hybrid commitment (please review):

1) Commitment structure (hybrid prepay + quarterly true-up):
   - Year 1: commit to initial slice of 4 GPUs with 25% prepay deposit (per Amphora request). Remaining Year-1 committed fees invoiced quarterly (25% at start of Q1, 25% at start of Q3) with a final true-up at year-end.
   - Ramp triggers: add slices at months 4 and 8 (6 GPUs each) contingent on quarterly utilization triggers OR by mutual written confirmation. The final slice (8 GPUs) scheduled for month 12 but may be deferred up to month 18 without penalty if utilization thresholds are not met.

2) Pricing / discounts:
   - Baseline annual prepay discount: 10% on committed units.
   - Multi-year (3-year upfront) blended: targeted 18% effective discount (previous sheet showed higher — we’ll cap at 18% to keep both sides comfortable).
   - If Amphora increases prepay above 60% of peak in year 1, Redwood will apply an additional 4% account credit to year-1 fees (reduced from the 5% originally proposed).

3) Overage & pool sharing:
   - Overage rate: list * 1.5 for short bursts (first 72 hours per quarter), list * 1.8 thereafter.
   - Reserved pool may be assigned across Amphora projects under a single account; usage-based quotas and tagging required for chargeback.

4) Operational notes and next steps:
   - We’ll produce a DocuSign term sheet that reflects the hybrid billing cadence and ramp-deferral clause.
   - Marissa (cc’d) will own billing schedule and can generate a sample invoice run for your review. Rishi will follow up on any legal redlines if needed.
   - Requested PO / signature by Dec 20 to lock pricing and capacity. If Amphora needs a shorter window, let us know and we can explore interim hold with a smaller deposit.

I’ll open a draft in HubSpot (AMP-437) and attach the revised term sheet — expecting to send for signature early next week. If you’re good with the compromise, please reply with confirmation and we’ll route to DocuSign.

Thanks — Neha
Head, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
